issues.quote: It has given me trouble for ten years and I have never let anyone near it, my uncle included.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the watch's reliability. It only gives the 8:40 reading at the nine o'clock strike.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a hint that the watch is erratic, so the 10:15, 10:18, 10:21 and 10:32 readings might be unreliable or drifting rather than a fixed offset. That is a doubt about the readings the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: He had been four years on that watch and he played it for anyone who would sit still.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the uncle's ownership of the repeater.
issues.misreading: The 'four years' is an extra duration detail. It is not a clock reading, but it adds a fact the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: I did not look at the watch. I did not want to know what it would say.
issues.fact: F2 says only that he did not look at his watch when the temple struck ten. The sheet does not say whether or when he checked it afterwards.
issues.misreading: Because he later gives precise readings by his watch (10:15, 10:18, 10:21, 10:32), a solver may wonder whether he looked at it between ten and 10:15, or whether the earlier readings were estimates. The sheet does not settle this.
